messages.content:
Aug/Sept.
Dear Parents,
Welcome to the preK 4s!  We are thrilled to start the year and get to know each of our Robins!  We are committed to doing all that we can to make our classroom a loving, safe, fun and fabulous learning environment for your children.   

School Supplies
Each student will be given a pencil box to be kept in the classroom.  The supplies that you send in will be kept in the boxes with any extras going to our general supplies. We will work with the children to help them recognize their names on their box and participate in caring for their items.  In addition, they will become responsible for getting their items when needed and putting them away appropriately when finished.

School Folders & Totes
Each student will receive a school folder and should have a tote to use daily.  The folder will house things for you to keep at home as well as those to send back in.  Please review your child’s folder each day after school.  It includes several helpful items, such as our daily schedule and school calendar.  Homework to be done, completed activities and crafts, newsletters, notes from us, etc. will all come to you via this folder. We also ask that a seasonally appropriate change of clothes be kept in your child’s tote throughout the year for spills or accidents.     

Water Bottles
Please send in a filled reusable water bottle labeled with your child’s name each day. These will be stored in our classroom to allow children to get drinks as needed and practice responsibility for their personal items.  

Homework & Reading Logs
Homework will be sent home on Mondays with the hope that it comes back to us by Thursday but can be turned in any day during our week.  These will be simple activities aimed at getting students in the “homework habit” and practicing the skills we are learning in school.  In addition to homework, students will have a monthly reading log in their folders.  For each book read, they color a picture on the page.  There are enough pictures for one to be colored each day of the month but will happily provide extra logs if a page is completed before the end of the month. 


Discipline & Rewards System
Individual behavior issues will be handled at the time that they occur.  We will focus on making good decisions and what that would look like in specific situations.  Should an issue be repetitive or concerning, I will reach out to make you aware and share with you how it was handled.  I will also be in touch to share great behavior as well.  Communications will be via notes in school folders or via email/phone depending on the occurrence.

My aim is to make our classroom a positive community.  We will have a class rewards system rather than daily individual behavior tracking.  Prior to dismissal, we will discuss how our day has gone and what we did well and where we have room for improvement.  Then, we’ll decide if our group behavior earned a puzzle piece on our bulletin board.  We will work toward completion of our puzzle and a class reward, such as pj day, treasure box trip, etc.  

Class Jobs
Our students will rotate through our class jobs each week.  We have 9 jobs, allowing our students to have a turn every other week.  This is another opportunity to encourage responsibility and participation in our class community.  Our jobs include attendance assistant, line leader, door holder, calendar commander, flag flyer, lucky
 librarian, weather watcher, table tidier, and clean up captain.

Class Parties & Birthdays
We will have several class parties throughout the year.  Sign ups for party supplies and volunteers will be sent and managed via SignUp Genius. Any additional details regarding costumes, special activities, etc. will be sent via our newsletters and email.  I also love to celebrate our Robin birthdays.  You are welcome to send in a special treat for snack time and/or a small something for the students. 

Special Days
Each of our Robins will have a special day that will take place during the second half of our school year.  We ask that you help your child complete and decorate a worksheet all about them.  Then you will get to come into Robin with your child for our morning circle time on that day.  They will get to share their poster with the class and bring or pick a book for you (or me) to read to the class. Additional information will be sent home later in the year and scheduling will take place via Sign Up Genius after winter break.
 
We are looking forward to a great year in the preK 4s!  Please don’t hesitate to reach out with questions, concerns and comments now and throughout the school year.

October
Robin 4’s Families,
What We’ve Been Up To
It’s been a wonderful start to the year! Each day the kids come in, place their totes on their assigned hooks, take their folders to our folder bucket, put their water bottles in our wall pockets and sit on the rug.  I’m thrilled with how quickly they’ve become comfortable with us and our classroom routines. 

Group Learning
We have been practicing our pencil and scissor grips. We’ve also been focusing on whole body listening and following directions. These skills are a challenge in a large group setting but the kids are making great strides.

Homework & Reading Logs
We greatly appreciate you reinforcing what we learn in class through the homework pages each week and reading to your kids regularly.  The kids are always so proud to show off their homework and colored reading logs.  We love praising all their efforts!  

Individual Focus
Each child works with me individually for a few minutes over the course of our play centers as time allows. We’re working on pencil grip, tracing their first names, as well as letter and number recognition.  It’s also a fun way to connect with each of them and get to know their personalities, skills, and interests. I’ll be sending home brief baseline assessments later this month with the information I gather during these sessions and throughout our class days. 

Looking Ahead
Our Harvest party will take place during class time on October 30th.  We can’t wait to see their costumes!
Our Sign Up Genius link for all party sign ups is still active with a handful of slots still open..  
If you’ve signed up, you are welcome to join us for the last hour of class that day. If you can’t make it, no worries! You’ll get to join us once we start special days later in the school year.

For Your Calendars
* 10/2 & 10/3 - No school
* 10/7 - Class PJ Day (once we fill our reward puzzle)
* 10/15 -  late arrival, Robin begins at normal times
* 10/23 - Fall Open House & Grandparents/Special People Celebration - 2’s & 3’s 6:15-6:45, 4’s & 5’s 6:45-7:15
* 10/28 - Some reptiles visits Robin!
* 10/30 - Harvest party in class - costumes encouraged!

November
Robin 4’s Families,
What We’ve Been Up To
Well, it’s never boring at preschool!  We’ve packed in a visit from reptiles, Bible stories with Ms. Rachel, family open house, a fabulous Harvest party with a costume fashion show and all kinds of fun.  And even with all of those extras, we’ve accomplished a ton of learning!  

Group Learning
At the start of school, we were adding name stickers to our classwork.  We’ve used the stickers as tracing guides while working to write first names.  I’ve made the font progressively lighter and lighter and early in October the “training wheels” came off!  We left the stickers off and they each write their names independently while using the name label on their crayon box as a visual reminder.  I was thrilled with everyone’s willingness to try and how well they all succeeded! Definitely a big step for our group!

Play Centers
Each week we reset our class into new play center groups to give everyone exposure to all their classmates.  We then rotate the groups daily through each of our 4 centers.  Usually the variety is welcomed and the kids find something to do in each area (because they’re all awesome centers) but sometimes they just aren’t interested in where they are assigned.  Several weeks ago, we instituted “always options”.  During play center time, reading a book or using our extensive collection of art supplies are our “always options”.  We have several creative souls who routinely opt to make cards or color.  Our routine serves us well but it’s been great seeing them choose and make the most of their play time.

For Your Calendars
Class Thanksgiving Feast - during class on 11/20
Thanksgiving break/No School - 11/24-11/28, Return 12/2
Class Christmas Party - during class on 12/16
Christmas program - 12/17 10:15 am 
Winter break/No School - 12/18-1/2, Return 1/5

And just a few reminders…Please clean out the “Keep at Home" side of your child’s folder each week.  There are always great things to find there!  And keep up with those reading logs!  The kids love to show their progress and we love rewarding them for it.

We thoroughly enjoy your kids each and every day, even on the crazy days!  They are making fabulous strides and it’s an honor to be on the journey with them.  As always, reach out with any questions or concerns. 

December
Robin 4’s Families,
How is it already December??!! As we weave in our holiday activities, we are continuing to encourage proper classroom behavior, following directions, good listening skills and kindness throughout our days. 

Christmas Donations for Elderly
To encourage the spirit of giving, our class will be collecting items for the residents at a skilled nursing facility.  This donation effort will take the place of a class book or gift exchange.  We will collect items from now until 12/11.  The kids will get to place them under our class tree and then we will be making cards to accompany the donated items.  Suggested items include but are not limited to blankets, grippy socks, lotion, soft baby dolls, stuffed animals, large print word searches, simple coloring books, crayons, and soft candy (Peppermint Patties/Reese's cups). 

Looking Ahead
Kindergarten registration in our area begins in late January with Robin registration shortly after in February. The early timelines can make the decision for the upcoming year challenging. Kindergarten is a fun and exciting step and our preK 5’s program is an amazing opportunity that allows additional time for social and academic progression. Two fabulous options! Some of you have already touched base with me about your plans but if you haven't, please know that I'm here to help. I'm happy to discuss my classroom observations and your child's progress. Just reach out!

For Your Calendar 
12/16 -Class Christmas party and PJ day - We’ll be having another PJ day with our 5’s friends as part of our festivities.  Yay!  
12/17 - Christmas Program -  The program begins at 10:15AM.  Please arrive at 10AM.  Children should wear their “Christmas best”.  All family and friends are welcome to attend.  Once we have our stage placement set, I will send out a diagram showing who will be where to help all of you choose seats with a good view of your child.
12/18-1/4 - Winter Break
1/5- First day back at Robin

Our days and hearts are full as we make our way into the holiday season!  As always, reach out with any questions or concerns. 




January
Robin Families,
We’re jumping right into the New Year with our usual routine and the addition of a few new things. One of those new additions will be special days. Below I have included a Signup Genius link for families to select a preferred day to come in for the first 30 minutes of our class. Each child will get to complete a provided poster and then share it with the class. A favorite book and snack to share are also welcomed. To get everyone in the swing of things, I will start us off with my own poster, snack, and favorite book next Monday : ) Sign up soon to get a date that works best for your family!


Along with special days, we will begin our class portfolios/big kid binders. On a weekly basis, we’ll bust out the binders to combine writing skills and imagination on the pages of these books. I love how this activity and the product showcase the kids’ individuality and progress. The process itself creates some of the best class conversations as they discuss what they’re creating and why. And the pride when they finally share them with their families…not to oversell it but seriously, it’s the best!

And it’s time for midyear evaluations! I’ll be working with the kids individually during play centers over the next few weeks to assess their progress with letter and number recognition, fine motor skills, age appropriate concepts, etc. If you are planning to apply as a tuition student or are unsure about pre-K 5’s versus kindergarten, please reach out to me if you haven’t already. I will focus on those evaluations first to ensure that information is available to you prior to the kindergarten registration window. For those that have already given me a heads up, I’ll have your child’s evaluations completed this week.

Dates for Your Calendar
1/5 - First Day Back to Robin
1/14 - Late Arrival 
1/19 - No School - MLK Jr. Day

February
Robin 4’s Families,
What We’ve Been Up To
A big step for our class has been the start of our portfolios/big kid binders. These are filled with pages of an alphabet book that they are individually creating.  We work on a page or two weekly.  These showcase their writing progress and creativity. The kids get super excited to get them out and to show what they have accomplished. 

We had a “coat clinic”.This was part of a class project for 2 high schoolers and turned into a fun activity for us. It included a relay race which had the whole crew chanting and encouraging each other. The flyer for the coat drive that you received previously is part of their project..

Next Up
We’ll be jumping into our individual rewards system - bucket filling! We’ve read the book, “Have You Filled a Bucket Today?”. It discusses how our positive actions can fill someone else’s bucket, which in turn fills ours. Doing good = feeling good. Now we’ll be applying it every day. This is a fun, visual way to reward individual positive behaviors. Each child has a bucket with their name on it on our window ledge and can earn pompoms throughout our day. This can be for something simple like listening the first time or helping a friend. Our teaching team watches closely to give lots of encouragement and pompoms. We’ve been known to give the kids hints or suggestions about how to earn them to make sure everyone is given a chance to be recognized. We’ll do “bucket checks” on Thursdays using our trusty ten frames and ten pompoms will earn a trip to the treasure chest. Since the pompoms are given to each child for different things, they’ll reach ten at different times, which can be tough the first few “bucket check” days. But this starts to be just another piece of our routine. Our message is that we know they are all “bucket fillers” and will have me restocking the treasure box all the time. And for those familiar with the book, we don’t “bucket dip”. The focus is all on the positive!

Special Days
Special days have begun!  Parents, other special adults, and siblings are invited to join us for the first half hour of our day.  Your Robin will get to share their “All About Me” page, which we will send home a few weeks in advance, and you’ll get to hang out for our circle time.  A special snack and a favorite book can be brought in as well. 

Valentine’s Day
Our Valentine’s Day party will be in class on 2/12. Treats and games and all the fun! We’d like for the kids to bring in valentines to exchange with each of their friends. We have 17 in our class. No need to address to each child since this actually makes passing them out super difficult in the time that we have.. But I’d love to see them all write their own names on what they are giving out.
   
Dates for Your Calendar
2/12 - Valentine’s Day Party  
2/16 - No School - Presidents’ Day
2/17-2/25 - Robin Priority Registration
2/18 - Late Arrival Day - Robin start times remain the same

Your kids have made such fantastic progress since we began in the fall. I’m looking forward to all the fun we have planned for the rest of the school year! As always, please reach out with any questions or concerns.

March
Robin Families,
What We’ve Been Up To
We are a room full of bucket fillers! The kids have embraced this idea and are making choices to earn those pom poms. I remind them that not every single good or expected behavior earns a pompom. I “catch” them along with the other teachers rather than when an action is done only for the reward. We’ve given pom poms for all kinds of things…helping a friend who drops their crayon box, pushing in chairs, sharing a book, following directions the first time, following our routine without reminders, being a good listener, using nice manners, trying to help when someone else is sad or mad, discussing a problem instead of reacting negatively, etc. Thursdays have become our “bucket check” days. I call each child over individually and they use a ten frame to count their pom poms. We figure out how many they have and how many more they need to go to the treasure chest. Since they are all earning pom poms for different things, the rewards come at different times. I have been thrilled with how the kids have accepted this idea. So many walk away excited by how close they are rather than disappointed that this isn’t their treasure box week. It’s become a fun part of our routine that has highlighted kindness, patience and maturity. Your kids are making me so proud!!

Upcoming
The first week of March we will be celebrating Read Across America and Dr. Seuss! On Wednesday, 3/4, we’ll have Wacky Wednesday/Silly Sock, Hair Or Whatever They Choose Day as our latest class reward.

Our annual Robin Spring Songfest will take place on Thursday, 3/19, at 6:45PM. Please arrive no earlier than 6:30 as the 3s class will be performing prior to our group. Ms. Laura has put together an adorable set of songs and the kids have already started rehearsing. All are welcome to join us at this event. 

Special Days
Special days have been such fun so far! The kids are great at being “on the spot” and sharing about themselves. The class is doing an excellent job listening and learning to ask questions. For those that still have this ahead, here’s a quick checklist: All About Me page, favorite snack and/or book (these are both optional).

Dates for Your Calendar
3/4 - Wacky Wednesday/Silly Sock, Hair, Whatever Day
3/18 - Late Arrival Day - Robin start times remain the same
3/19 - 4s/5s Spring Songfest 6:45pm, arrive 6:30pm
4/2 - In-class Easter party - 10:30am-11:30am
4/6-4/10 - Spring Break
4/13 - Return to Robin

As always, please reach out with any questions or concerns!

April
Robin 4’s Families,
What We’ve Been Up To
Bucket filling, special days, a leprechaun visit, Spring Songfest, getting ready for our walking field trips, etc. Never a dull day in our class!
 
Upcoming
And it’s April! This month will be filled with spring and Easter-themed fun! We’ll celebrate our 100th school day on Tuesday, 4/15 followed by our Easter party on Thursday, 4/17. As part of our Easter fun, we will be playing What’s in My Egg?. Each child will come home with an empty egg and egg clue sheet in a plastic bag with their name on it.  Please help your child fill their egg with a mystery item of their choosing, create 3 clues on the sheet, and return it in the provided bag no later than 4/16. This is a great opportunity for the kids to practice talking in front of the class and using their critical thinking skills to solve the mystery item in each egg. We’ll be playing a preview version of the game this week to introduce that idea.

With the end of the year quickly approaching, I’ll be working on final assessments. These include social and academic information. Quite a bit is collected through observation and I use games and activities to individually assess things like letter and number recognition, spatial concepts, etc. Please bear in mind that mastery of everything listed on the evaluation is not the expectation. I am definitely of the “progress versus perfection” mindset. Your kids have all made great strides this year and wow me with the connections they make and big thoughts that they share. The assessments are just the details with the big picture always being that your kids are awesome!

More celebrations are coming! We’d love to see all of you while we hang out at the park on 5/13. For those children that are moving onto kindergarten, we’ll have a combined graduation with the 5s class on 5/14. All family members are welcome at these celebrations.

Dates for Your Calendar
4/14 - Walking field trip to local coffee house
4/16 - Send in What’s in my Egg? & Clues 
4/17 - Class Easter Party
4/29 - Walking field trip to local fire station 
5/13 - Last day of class
5/14 - Park Day  11:30AM-12:30PM - All family members welcome
5/15 - Graduation 9:30AM - All family members welcome

May
Robin 4’s Families,
As we make our way to the finish line, here are just a few reminders…

5/1 - Evaluations come home - They have all made such amazing progress this year. It’s been such fun seeing them confidently show me all that they have learned. Please reach out with any questions as you review the assessments.

5/12 & 5/13 - Last days of class - We’ll be sending home completed portfolios (Get ready! These are amazing!), as well as your child’s leftover supplies. I will have a bin at the bottom of the steps at dismissal if you’d like to donate any of their supplies back to our classroom for the art center.

5/14 - Park Day  11:30AM-12:30PM - For all students and family members. Fingers crossed for good weather and that our caterpillars will have emerged and be ready for release. 

5/15 - Graduation 9:30AM - For graduating Robins and family members. We ask that our graduates arrive at 9:10 in their celebration clothes. We’ll meet you at the Welcome Center doors to gather our class together. 

It's been a fantastic year! I can hardly believe how much we've accomplished and shared. Your kids have made Robin a better and brighter place. Thank you for sharing them with us!



Task:
 These are my class newsletters for the current year. Could you give me suggestions to streamline the format on a monthly basis?

Of course! It's wonderful that you are so thorough and communicative with your families. Streamlining the format will make your newsletters even more effective by making them easier for busy parents to scan and digest. The key is to create a consistent structure that you can use each month.

Here are some suggestions for a streamlined monthly newsletter format, based on the content you've already provided.

### Proposed Monthly Newsletter Template

You can create a simple template in a word processor or email client. Here’s a recommended structure:

**Header**
*   **Month & Year:** e.g., "Robin 4's Newsletter - October 202X"
*   **A Warm Greeting:** A short, friendly opening. (e.g., "Hello Robin Families!")

**Section 1: Learning Highlights**
*(Combine "What We've Been Up To," "Group Learning," and "Individual Focus")*
*   Use bullet points or short paragraphs.
*   Highlight 2-3 key academic or social skills you're focusing on.
*   Mention any special projects, visitors, or milestones.
    *   *Example:* "We've been practicing our pencil grips and have started writing our first names independently!"

**Section 2: Upcoming Events & Important Dates**
*(This is the most critical section for parents to reference. Make it a clear, bulleted list.)*
*   Use bold for dates.
*   Include parties, holidays, no-school days, special visitors, and performances.
    *   *Example:*
        *   **Oct 7:** Class PJ Day
        *   **Oct 23:** Fall Open House (6:45-7:15 PM)
        *   **Oct 30:** Harvest Party (Costumes Encouraged!)

**Section 3: Reminders & Announcements**
*(A dedicated space for ongoing tasks and new information.)*
*   Use bullet points.
*   Include things like:
    *   Homework & reading log due dates.
    *   Supply needs (e.g., seasonal clothes in totes).
    *   Requests for volunteers or donations.
    *   Explanation of new systems (like the "bucket filling" system).
    *   Quick tips (e.g., "Please clean out the 'Keep at Home' side of folders weekly.")

**Section 4: A Peek Ahead**
*(Optional but fun section to build excitement.)*
*   Briefly describe a fun theme or activity for the upcoming month.
    *   *Example:* "In November, we'll be exploring the story of the first Thanksgiving and starting our class gratitude journal."

**Closing**
*   A warm sign-off.
*   Consistent contact information (email/phone).
*   An invitation to reach out with questions.

---

### Formatting Tips for Readability

*   **Use Headings:** Clear titles for each section (like the ones above) help parents navigate.
*   **Use Bullet Points:** Break up lists of dates, reminders, or learning goals. This makes information scannable.
*   **Bold Key Information:** Bold important dates, new policy names (like "bucket filling"), and action items (e.g., "**Send in What's in my Egg? by 4/16**").
*   **Keep Paragraphs Short:** Large blocks of text can be intimidating. Aim for 2-3 sentences per paragraph.
*   **Use White Space:** Don't be afraid of empty space. It makes the document feel less cluttered.

### Content Strategy

*   **Create a "Welcome Packet":** The information in your August/September letter (school supplies, folders, discipline philosophy) is foundational. Consider turning this into a one-time "Welcome to PreK 4s" packet that goes home at the start of the year. Then, your monthly newsletters can refer back to it, rather than repeating it.
*   **Maintain Your Voice:** Your newsletters have a warm, enthusiastic tone. Keep that! The template is just a framework to organize your excellent content.

By adopting a consistent format, you'll make it easier for parents to find the information they need, which strengthens the home-school connection. Your newsletters are already a fantastic resource; this will just make them even better!

Be sure to clearly identify where those references are found.
